public_rationale: DeepSeek provides a pre-post counterexample under the ordinary reading. Its May 2024 paper documents substantial model training and deployed inference. The accompanying historical records identify High-Flyer as its parent, financier, and source of computing resources. A wealthy private backer outside Google, Amazon, and Microsoft still contradicts the claim that no private startup could build and scale an LLM without those three. This does not establish that entering the market was cheap or easy.
limitations: The independence finding combines a contemporary technical paper with later reporting and historical testimony.
The result depends on treating material financing and compute dependence as the meaning of help.
The evidence establishes substantial model development and deployment, not parity with the largest provider's customer base.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No private startup can afford to build and scale an LLM without the help of Google, Amazon or Microsoft.
conditions: without help of Google, Amazon or Microsoft

statement.excerpt: No private startup can actually afford to build and scale a Large Language Model without the help of Google, Amazon or Microsoft — and thus they would, assuming they actually became useful, effectively control every single product involving this technology.

from_speaker: afford to build and scale a Large Language Model
without the help of Google, Amazon or Microsoft
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a universal claim of necessary financial or computing dependence on at least one of the three named companies.
A privately financed startup qualifies even if its founder or parent business is wealthy. The source does not exclude such startups.
Building and scaling means training a substantial competitive model and deploying inference, not merely announcing a model or fine-tuning someone else's small model.
Help means material funding or computing infrastructure necessary for development and deployment. Incidental use of ordinary software or public research is not effective dependence.
For the ongoing state, use the latest completed calendar quarter before publication: April through June 2024.
No particular company's financial amount or accounting measure is asserted, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Comprehensive evidence shows that private startups developing and deploying substantial LLMs necessarily depended on funding or compute from Google, Amazon, or Microsoft.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one private startup trained and deployed a substantial competitive LLM using independently identified financing and infrastructure outside the three named companies.

evidence.explanation: The paper documents DeepSeek-V2's 236-billion-parameter model, substantial pretraining, and deployed inference on H800 hardware. Together with the independently identified High-Flyer resources in e2 and e3, this supplies a counterexample already operating before the post.

evidence.explanation: The surrounding historical account traces DeepSeek's infrastructure and research funding to High-Flyer from its 2023 founding. This supports continuity of an independently financed route into the May 2024 model release.
